newsitem.title: USA: L.A. food worker had "false positive" for hepatitis.
newsitem.headline: L.A. food worker had "false positive" for hepatitis.

text.p: A food service worker in the Los Angeles school system believed to have contracted hepatitis A from eating tainted strawberries does not have the disease, a schools spokesman said Wednesday.
Meanwhile, health officials in Missouri said the tainted fruit may also have been shipped to Kansas and Missouri.
Earlier this month, thousands of schoolchildren in Michigan, Georgia and Los Angeles were inoculated against the hepatitis A virus, which was also traced to Arizona, Iowa and Tennessee.

Los Angeles schools spokesman Brad Sales said health officials got a "false positive" when the man was first screened for exposure to the hepatitis A virus, along with 10 other school kitchen workers last month.
"A large number of adults, some 30 percent, are exposed at some time (in their life) to the virus and build up an immunity," he said.
When a second, more specific test was carried out, the man was found not to have an active case of hepatitis A, said Sales, a spokesman for the Los Angeles Unified School District.

The scare broke out on April 2 when Michigan state health officials said that 150 students and teachers there had contracted hepatitis A from eating the frozen strawberries, which originated in Mexico, as part of a U.S. Department of Agriculture-sponsored school meals program.
Los Angeles, which also served the suspect strawberries, inoculated than 9,000 schoolchildren and teachers on April 4. None has developed hepatitis A.

The Missouri Department of Health said Wednesday a Kansas company also sold the fruit to three Missouri wholesale food distributors, and that it was working to identify institutions such as hospitals, schools and restaurants that may have purchased the suspect product.
"We are not aware of any illnesses associated with the consumption of these strawberries (in Missouri) at this time," a department spokeswoman said.
Officials said the strawberries were sent to Packers Food Products Inc of Edwardsville, Kansas, which later sold them to Missouri distributors.
Packers has initiated a voluntary recall of the strawberries from distributors, the department said. The strawberries in question were sold to distributors between last summer and December 1996.
